findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded as plaintext Lambda environment variables (access_key = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", secret_key = "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"), and are also stored in Terraform state. Anyone with read access to the function configuration, the console, or the state file obtains long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables are encrypted only with the AWS-managed default key rather than a customer-managed CMK, providing no control over key policy, rotation, or access to the values.
The function uses runtime "nodejs12.x", an end-of-life runtime that no longer receives security patches, so known Node.js vulnerabilities will remain unpatched.

The execution role has no attached or inline permission policies at all, leaving the function with no defined least-privilege permission set; any permissions granted out-of-band (e.g. via a broad managed policy attached outside this configuration) would be unbounded and unauditable.
